messages:
anya (product): Kicking off a PRD intake for a customer ask from AcmeCorp — they need tenant-aware model routing + safe rollback controls. I want to capture problem, goals, non-goals, success metrics, acceptance criteria, and edge cases so we can size and prioritize.

matt (eng): quick Q: is this primarily a routing + policy surface (pin tenant -> model) or does Acme also expect separate caches/instances per tenant?

anya (product): Problem statement: Acme runs a multi-tenant app and wants deterministic routing of inference requests per-tenant to pinned model variants (and quantization levels) for compliance/testing. They also need automatic fallback when capacity or perf regressions happen and an automated safe-rollback path. Not asking for full per-tenant infra isolation.

katie (design): Goals: 1) UI + API for pinning a tenant to a model variant; 2) clear rollout controls (canary %, time window); 3) visible reasons for fallback and rollback; 4) lightweight tenant-level telemetry (latency, token cost, quality regressions).

diego (solutions): Non-goals (to avoid scope creep): 1) full per-tenant hardware isolation (Dedicated pools still separate effort); 2) custom per-tenant model training or finetuning flows; 3) complex billing changes — we surface usage only.

jess (cs): Success metrics from Acme: reduce incidents tied to unexpected model changes to 0 for pinned tenants, <200ms added p95 latency for pinned routing, ability to rollback within 5 minutes with <1% error spike. They want a canary to block rollout if quality drops >2% on eval set.

matt (eng): Acceptance criteria (engineering): - API: POST /tenants/:id/pinning -> model_id + variant + start/end optional. - Router: consistent sticky routing for in-flight KV cache correctness. - Fallback: policy config that can fallback to a compatible variant or smaller quantized model automatically. - Rollback: single-button rollback (console) triggers immediate route flip and invalidates relevant prefix cache. - Telemetry: tenant-level latency/cost/quality per model for the last 30d.

katie (design): UI acceptance: - Pin management table with status (pinned, canary, fallback). - Canary control modal (pct, duration, eval set link). - One-click rollback with confirmation and visible reason.

diego (solutions): Edge cases to call out: - model variant incompatible with request shape (e.g., different tokenizer) -> failover rules. - KV cache poisoning if we switch mid-session -> how do we preserve session consistency? - Long-running streaming calls during rollback. - Cross-tenant rate-limit spikes if many tenants pinned to expensive variants.

matt (eng): Technical notes: we need model compatibility metadata (tokenizer id, max seq) to validate pin requests. Router must support atomic route flip per-tenant; KV cache invalidation needs TTL/namespace per-tenant or a versioned prefix. Canary implementation can reuse existing rollout infra but need tenant scoping.

anya (product): Timeline asks: Acme wants an initial beta in ~8 weeks for limited tenants. Proposed MVP scope: API + console pinning, basic fallback policy, telemetry, rollback button. No per-tenant hardware.

lucy (sales): Acme is willing to sign a pilot SOW if we can commit to beta in that window and provide a rollback SLA for pinned tenants.

matt (eng): Rough risk list: cache correctness, complexity in router state, extra load on smaller models when fallback triggers, billing attribution work. Need eng estimate: 4-6 sprints across runtime + console + telemetry.

anya (product): Ask: volunteers for owners: eng runtime owner (matt), console owner (katie), solutions + cs for pilot (diego/jess). Can everyone ack and I’ll convert to a PRD skeleton?

matt (eng): ack.

katie (design): ack — will sketch UI flows tomorrow.

diego (solutions): ack, will collect Acme's eval set and tokenizer details.

jess (cs): ack — I'll prep pilot success checklist with Acme and capture required SLOs.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy window created for feature branch staging: 2025-10-03 02:00 UTC (placeholder).

anya (product): thanks — I'll draft the PRD skeleton (problem/goals/non-goals/metrics/acceptance/risks/timeline) and ping for review early next week. If anyone thinks a non-goal above should move to goal, call it out now.

lucy (sales): one more ask from Acme: allow export of tenant-level telemetry CSVs for audits. Add as low-priority acceptance if feasible.

matt (eng): noted — CSV export is straightforward once telemetry backfills exist; mark as nice-to-have for MVP+1.

anya (product): great. wrapping up — next: I'll post the PRD link when ready. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
